title: How Markets Shape Values and Political Preferences: A Field Experiment

reviewed_pages.boundary_basis: The supplied PDF has 20 pages; printed pagination runs continuously from 473 through 492, beginning with title/abstract and ending with references. No embedded supplement or appendix pages occur.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–20 (printed 473–492), including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Appendix pointers, verification materials, SI, and external sources were excluded as evidence.

experiments.name: Six-week multi-arm financial-market engagement field experiment (including 12-month follow-up)
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary causal study. All seven arms/subarms were assigned in one participant-level block randomization; the one-year follow-up reused the original assignment and therefore belongs to this experiment.

design_map.label: Exact treatment and comparator
design_map.value: Control: surveys only. Asset arms: six weekly allocations of £50 among three assets, no cash, with 10% weekly portfolio penalty for missed decisions; real stocks, sports-indexed assets, or non-incentivized fantasy stocks. Exact firms, teams, and all platform materials NR in main article.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; compares the two eligible experiments. Cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: The Swedish and U.S. co-primary experiments have the same reporting architecture and therefore the same criterion scores. Country-specific field dates, sample sources, n values, and selected numerical results differ, but neither experiment reports representation allocation probabilities, sequence generation, a fully reconstructable estimator, weighting status, error-bar construction, missingness rules, or complete numerical effects with uncertainty.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, figures, figure labels, table/figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figures 2–7 earned credit for displayed sample sizes and group quantities. They did not earn inference credit because no note or prose defines the vertical bars. Appendix/SI pointers were treated only as evidence that information is outside the permitted source, never as evidence that omitted details were reported.

checks.treatment: Credited printed country n values and visible response distributions exactly as prose evidence would be credited.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. In particular, in-article Table A1 earned credit for outcome, model columns, covariates, effects, standard errors, clustering, and N. Figure 5 earned credit for plotted AMCEs and 95% intervals, but its pointer to SI did not supply omitted exact values or marginal means. Appendix/registry pointers never earned credit for missing content.

title: Policy Deliberation and Voter Persuasion: Experimental Evidence from an Election in the Philippines
page_boundary_note: The supplied PDF contains the complete 16-page published main article. PDF pages 1–15 contain article text, figures, tables, notes, footnotes, conclusion, and references; PDF page 16 ends the references and lists titles of online Supporting Information only. experiments.name: Barangay-level randomized deliberative campaign experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment: 39 barangays were assigned within 13 municipalities to a town-hall deliberative campaign or business-as-usual campaigning. Official-election outcomes and the two-week post-election survey are analyses/follow-up measurements of the same original assignment, not separate experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, main-text tables, figures, and their notes received identical evidentiary status. execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figures, table/figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 6 supplied wave interview counts and field information; footnotes 15–19 supplied estimand labels, attribute levels, and the z-test formula; figure notes supplied significance-shading rules. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared outside prose. Conversely, appendix pointers and citations did not fill main-article omissions.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison only; this independent session contains one paper, so cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.summary: All three conjoint experiments report attributes, task counts, focal AMCE plots, two-way clustering, and k-sensitivity. The network-census candidate study is a supporting replication on a separate sample. Statistical transparency is essentially the same across experiments: exact randomization mechanics, outcome coding, full model specification, analyzed N, missingness rules, and interval construction are absent. The neighbor experiment additionally reports a lower-power warning but no exact focal contrast.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison only; cross-paper synthesis is reserved for the later independent-assessment stage.
direct_comparison.summary: Study 1 is clearer about its respondent-level analysis, ITT estimand, model columns, Ns, coefficients, and standard errors. Study 2 is clearer about recruitment exclusions, attrition, repeated tasks, and respondent clustering, but its conjoint ACIE computation, fitted analysis unit, assignment probabilities/restrictions, model-specific observation counts, and interval construction are not reconstructable from the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as coequal evidence. Table 3 earned credit for OLS, outcome, controls, comparison condition, Ns, estimates, and standard errors; Figure 2 earned credit for visible contrasts, reference levels, plotted effects, and uncertainty bars. Credit was withheld only where those displays and notes jointly remained incomplete (for example SE type in Study 1 and confidence level/construction in Study 2). Appendix pointers were not treated as evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

title: Brokers, Social Networks, Reciprocity, and Clientelism

reviewed_pages.boundary_finding: The PDF contains the complete 18-page published main article. PDF page 1 begins the title/abstract and printed page 795; PDF page 18 ends the references and carries only a notice naming online supporting-information appendices, not their contents. All 18 PDF pages were reviewed.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–18 (printed 795–812), including main-text prose, equations, figures, tables, notes, and footnotes. Online supporting information, preregistration, verification materials, code, and cited external works were excluded as evidence.
inventory_conclusion: No distinct randomized treatment-effect experiment is reported in the published main article. Random selection of survey targets is sampling, not treatment assignment. The trust game supplies a measured covariate; the main article reports no randomized manipulation or treatment contrast for it.
scope_exclusion_note: No list-experiment measurement design is described in the published main article. A reference-list citation to a list-experiment method is not a study in this paper, and Appendix C is only named in an online-SI notice whose contents are outside scope.

experiments.name: Survey and family-network analyses of broker selection, knowledge, targeting, monitoring, enforcement, and vote choice
experiments.classification_rationale: The article expressly tests observational implications. Network position, reciprocity, handout receipt/offers, perceptions, and vote reports are measured rather than randomized. Random sampling of voters or names does not create treatment and control arms.

criterion_definitions.wording: Population and recruitment: Target population, eligibility, recruitment, and major exclusions are fully reported.
Experimental conditions: Treatment and comparator, or all randomized attributes and levels, are reported precisely enough to reproduce.
Randomization: Unit, probabilities or ratio, sequence-generation process, and restrictions are fully reported.
Outcome measurement: Outcomes, coding, timing, and primary or secondary status are fully reported.
Participant flow: Numbers recruited, randomized, exposed, followed, and analyzed are reported as applicable.
Estimand: The causal or descriptive quantity being estimated is explicitly defined.
Estimator/model: The statistical operation used to estimate the estimand is reconstructable from the text, table, or table notes.
Analysis unit: The reader can determine whether observations are participants, profiles, choices, sessions, or another unit.
Coding and reference categories: Treatment coding, outcome coding, omitted categories, and reference levels are explicit.
Specification: Covariates, fixed effects, weights, transformations, and column-to-column specification changes are explicit.
Dependence and inference: Standard errors, clustering, repeated-observation dependence, bootstrap or permutation procedures, and confidence-interval construction are explicit.
Missingness and attrition: Inclusion rules, missing outcomes, exclusions, attrition, and corresponding adjustments are explicit.
Multiplicity and analysis status: Multiple-testing procedures and prespecified versus exploratory analyses are distinguished.
Analysis sample: The number of observations used in each focal analysis is reported.
Group quantities: Relevant control means, treatment means, marginal means, or other raw quantities are reported.
Effect and uncertainty: Effect estimates and standard errors or confidence intervals are reported.
Model-to-result traceability: Each focal numerical result can be connected directly to a particular outcome, contrast, specification, sample, and inference procedure.
Robustness analyses: Alternative specifications and sensitivity analyses are explained sufficiently to understand what changed.
Internal-validity threats: Attrition, noncompliance, spillovers, demand effects, measurement problems, and other relevant threats are discussed.
Inferential scope: The paper distinguishes the randomized contrast from broader claims about mechanisms, populations, and settings.

additional_checklist.status: Omitted as instructed because no additional checklist was supplied.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.

rows.statistical_transparency_finding: No randomized experiment can be reconstructed because none is reported. The observational tables identify many model features, but the trust-game construction and survey recruitment details are delegated to excluded SI.

findings: Main-text tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, equations, prose, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status.
Table notes supplied analysis units, observation counts, clustering, fixed effects, and control information for the observational inventory map; these were credited exactly as prose would have been.
No score was reduced merely because information appeared in a display rather than prose.
Pointers to SI Sections B/D and SI Tables/Figures were recorded as pointers only and were not treated as supplying omitted details.
Random sampling of survey respondents or quiz targets was not conflated with randomized treatment assignment.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

direct_comparison.summary: The two supporting experiments have the same criterion profile. Table 5 makes their OLS results unusually traceable at the result level, but neither experiment is fully reconstructable because randomization probabilities/sequence, exact treatment wording, full specification, dependence procedure, and missing-case flow are omitted. The 2018 study is somewhat clearer about setting scope because it explicitly discusses counterfactual signals and debriefing; this does not change its binary Criterion 20 score because population scope remains unbounded.

rows.finding: The experimental task and focal logistic/prediction estimand are relatively clear, but full vignettes, randomization mechanics, per-analysis N, reference categories, base SE procedure, missing-data rules, and analysis status are not reconstructable.
The displayed minimum-wage manipulation, outcomes, OLS family, and graphical estimates are clear; other issue vignettes and several implementation/inference details remain outside the main article.
Least reconstructable statistically: the article relies on 'replication' wording, does not restate the model/specification, and reports conflicting focal sample sizes (1,664 vs 1,816).

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figure 1 supported the shown gun-control manipulation; Figures 2–6 and their notes supported displayed estimands, point estimates, and 95% intervals. Footnotes 9–11 supported sample/model details. Pointers to Supporting Information were not credited for omitted content. No main-text regression tables were present.

rows.summary: Strong visible result reporting, but randomization, complete specification, missingness, and scope details are insufficient for full reconstruction.
Only pooled attention/recall percentages are reported; sample, arm contrasts, model, and inference are absent.

findings: Tables, figure notes, table notes, footnotes, and prose were treated as equal main-article evidence.
Figure 4/5 arm means, Ns, confidence intervals, and contrast p-values received full evidentiary credit where they directly supplied a required element.

Table 2 and its note received full credit for the linear estimator, coefficient/SE reporting, column samples, and iteration-level clustering; missing or inconsistent adjustment details were not inferred.
Pointers to the SI Appendix, preanalysis plan, and verification archive were recorded but never used to fill omitted information.
Absence judgments were checked across PDF pages 1–16 and the relevant displays; no invented quotation was used for an absence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment-level comparison; cross-paper synthesis is reserved for the later independent-assessment stage.
direct_comparison.finding: Studies 2 and 3 are substantially more transparent than the diagnostic Studies 4 and 5 because they print models, dependence structure, and numerical uncertainty. Even Studies 2 and 3 are not fully reconstructable: allocation/sequence details, full stimulus wording, outcome/reference coding, inference construction, missing-data rules, per-analysis observation counts, raw condition quantities, and complete attrition-threat discussion are incomplete. Study 2 meets 7/20 core items and Study 3 meets 6/20; Study 4 meets 1/20 and Study 5 meets 2/20.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figure 4's note earned evidence for model family, random/fixed effects, and 95% intervals. Figure examples did not earn credit for omitted complete stimulus sets. Pointers to supporting information or replication materials did not supply missing information.
checks: Figure 4 note credited for linear mixed-effects models, participant random effects, vignette fixed effects, and 95% CI error bars.
Footnotes 10, 11, and 14 credited for analysis status and exclusions.
Figure 3 and Figure 5 credited as examples only, not as complete treatment documentation.
Supporting-information pointers on printed pages 783, 785, 787, and 790 were not treated as evidence of the omitted content.

direct_comparison.finding: Within this article, all three experiments precisely report conditions and plotted effects. The vignette model is clearer than the conjoint models about estimator family; all three omit analysis-specific N, attrition/missingness rules, and full CI construction. The two conjoint experiments additionally omit attribute assignment probabilities and regression family/link, while clearly reporting respondent clustering.

consistency_audit.finding: Prose, tables, figures, table notes, and figure notes received equal evidentiary status. Table 3 earned condition credit; Tables 4–5 earned attribute/level credit; Figures 3–9 and their notes earned coding, reference-category, clustering, effect, and uncertainty credit. Appendix pointers earned no credit for omitted content.
checks: Table and figure notes were cited as positive evidence where they supplied required details.

experiments.name: 1990–1992 and 1992–1994–1996 NES panel analyses
experiments.classification_rationale: Observational analysis: no new randomized assignment; cross-lagged OLS models relate measured welfare feelings and racial predispositions over time.

additional_checklist.note: No additional reporting checklist was supplied; separate checklist scoring is omitted.

direct_comparison.finding: All three experiments precisely report vignette content and focal slope differences, but none reports complete randomization procedures, model-specific Ns, variance-estimator details, or full focal model specifications in the main article. The 1991 experiment is relatively more transparent because it names base covariates and describes placebo/robustness checks; the 2014 and 2015 models rely more heavily on excluded SI pointers.

findings: Main-text prose, figure notes, footnotes, and Table 1 notes were given equal evidentiary status.
Figure-note interaction t statistics earned uncertainty credit just as prose p values did.
No credit was withheld merely because evidence appeared in a display or note.
Conversely, Figures 1–3 do not contain model Ns, complete specifications, standard-error methods, or raw arm means; pointers to SI tables were not treated as supplying those facts.
Table 1 was inspected visually and used only to classify the NES panel work as observational; it was not scored as an experiment.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; comparison is across the three scored experiments. Cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: E1 and E2 have the same visible model reporting strengths (OLS label, analysis unit, per-column N, coefficients, and SEs) and the same key gaps (randomization, coding, SE computation, missingness, multiplicity). E3 is substantially less transparent because only a directional claim and appendix pointer appear in the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1, its note, figure/table notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Table 1 earned credit for OLS identification, per-column sample sizes, coefficients, standard errors, dependent-variable range/direction, and field fixed effects. It did not earn credit for details the table and note omit, including allocation, treatment pooling, reference categories, SE computation, clustering, and missing-data rules. Appendix pointers supplied no omitted information.
table_note_examples: Criterion 7 estimator component credited from the Table 1 note.
Criterion 14 credited from Table 1 observation rows.
Criterion 16 credited from Table 1 coefficient and SE cells.
Criterion 11 remained zero because 'associated standard errors' does not identify their computation.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

title: The Variable Persuasiveness of Political Rhetoric

reviewed_pages.boundary_basis: PDF page 1 begins the title/abstract and printed page 255; PDF page 16 ends the references and lists online Supporting Information on printed page 270. The listed appendices are not embedded in the PDF and were excluded.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–16 (printed 255–270), including main-text figures, notes, and footnotes. Online appendices, verification materials, and all external sources were excluded.

inventory_summary.notes: No list-experiment measurement design, unreported-outcome pilot, diagnostic randomization separate from the two experiments, or observational study was identified. direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment comparison; only one paper is in this independent session.
direct_comparison.summary: Experiment 1 is more statistically transparent because Equations 1–4 identify its ordered Bradley–Terry hierarchy, coding, analysis unit, and a main-text controlled robustness model. Experiment 2 clearly defines the policy-specific difference in means but omits the right-panel association model, arm-by-issue sample sizes, outcome recode, dependence adjustment, and interval construction. Neither experiment is fully reconstructable from the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figure content, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Credit was awarded from Figure 1/4 prompt wording, Equations 1–5, Figure 2/3/5 notes, and footnotes where they supplied components. Appendix pointers and the Supporting Information list were treated only as evidence that information is outside the main article, never as evidence that the omitted information was reported.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as coequal main-article evidence. Table 1 earned credit for labeled arms, providers, and sample sizes; figure notes earned credit for OLS, standardization, broad contrasts, plotted estimates, and confidence intervals. They did not earn credit for omitted details such as exact stimulus/outcome wording, allocation probabilities, complete coding, model specifications, per-model Ns, standard-error procedures, or CI construction. Appendix pointers were treated only as evidence that information was outside scope.

records.example: Table 1 supports treatment labels and experiment-level sample sizes.
Figures 1–5 support plotted effects/CIs, OLS descriptions, standardization, and stated baselines.
Pointers to instrumentation, recruitment details, regression tables, and robustness checks did not fill main-article omissions.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment comparison only; cross-paper synthesis is deferred because this session contains one paper.
direct_comparison.finding: The three primary experiments have the same criterion-level transparency profile: estimands and respondent analysis units are identifiable and effects/CIs are plotted, but exact stimuli/outcomes, allocation, complete coding/specification, inference details, per-model samples, missingness, multiplicity, and population scope are not reconstructable from the main article.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper session; comparison is between the two scored experiments, not across papers.
direct_comparison.summary: Both experiments fully report vignette conditions and graphical group quantities/effects. Study 1 adds a preregistration statement and a 2×2 reputation manipulation; Study 2 reports partial exclusion rules and a four-arm replication/extension. Neither reports allocation probabilities/sequence generation, per-analysis Ns, full coding/specifications, or bootstrap/CI construction, so their core subtotal profiles are identical.

findings: Tables 1 and 2 received full evidentiary status for exact treatment and comparator text.
Figures 2–7 and their notes received full evidentiary status for plotted means, effect estimates, model labels, confidence intervals, and broad analysis descriptions.
No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.
Display notes did not receive extra credit when they named OLS, bootstrap, or mediation without enough implementation detail to reconstruct the analysis.
Pointers to appendices, preregistration, and verification materials were treated only as pointers; omitted content was not credited.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

experiments.name: Cross-sectional study of political experience, gender, attitudes, and incentivized behavioral tasks
experiments.classification_rationale: One sample of 400 incoming and outgoing gram-panchayat politicians completed a survey and six behavioral tasks. The main-text analyses compare naturally occurring gender and political-experience groups. The article explicitly calls the study observational. Random die outcomes, a 50/50 risky payoff, anonymous matching, or designation of game roles are features of measurement/payoff implementation; none is an analyzed randomized intervention or causal treatment contrast. The survey, die-tossing, dictator, trust, ultimatum, public-goods-with-punishment, and investment tasks are therefore measurements within this one observational study, not distinct randomized experiments.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.statistical_transparency: The treatment texts, arm counts, outcome questions, timing, adjusted arm predictions, and focal p-values are visible in the main article. Reconstruction fails chiefly because assignment generation/probabilities, exact model/covariates, analysis Ns, missing-data rules, and inference/error-bar construction are not reported.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1 and its note, Figure 6 and its note, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 earned full treatment-text evidence; Figure 6 earned group-quantity evidence but not estimator/inference credit because its note does not identify the model, covariate set, error bars, or CI construction. Appendix pointers supplied no evidence.
findings: Table 1 and its note establish exact prime wording, the no-prime comparator, mutually exclusive exposure, and realized arm counts.
Figure 6 and its note establish adjusted arm predictions and that covariates were held at means; they do not establish which covariates, the model/link, or the meaning of error bars.
The democracy result is p=.049 in prose for the original scale but p=.064 in Figure 6 after dichotomization (footnote 8); both were retained without treating them as the same specification.
For violence, prose on printed p. 522 reports p=.005 while Figure 6 reports p=.009; this display/text discrepancy is flagged for human review.
References to the online appendix, preregistration, and results available from authors were not credited.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; comparison is between its two scored experiments, not a cross-paper synthesis.
direct_comparison.findings: Wave 2 and wave 3 have the same criterion profile (6/20): both clearly report the focal estimand, estimator family, participant analysis unit, focal sample sizes, effects/95% intervals, and inferential scope. Neither fully reports exact stimuli, randomization implementation, factor scoring, variance/CI construction, missingness, multiplicity, or reproducible robustness checks. Wave 3 more directly discusses the outcome-wording measurement problem, but this does not change criterion 19 because other validity threats remain unaddressed.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Figure notes earned credit for models, sample sizes, contrasts, and 95% intervals; Table 2 earned credit for item wording; Tables 3–4 earned credit for loadings/reliability. consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figures, figure notes, tables, table notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status when they were inside the published main article. Figure 7/8 labels and notes earned credit for levels, references, effect estimates, and 95% CIs. Table 4 and its note were used for inventory/context but did not convert the RDD into a randomized experiment. Pointers to Supporting Information were recorded only as evidence that details are absent from the permitted source, never as substantive evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

findings: Main-text tables, table notes, figure notes, footnotes, and prose were given equal evidentiary status.
Table 1 and its note earned full credit for estimator/model, analysis unit, analysis N, effect/uncertainty, traceability, and the displayed robustness sequence where jointly unambiguous.
No credit was withheld merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.
Pointers to online supporting information were recorded only as pointers and never treated as evidence that omitted details were reported.
Absence judgments were based on all 16 PDF pages, with focused review of design/results on PDF pages 5–13 and the supporting-information boundary on PDF page 16.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper session; cross-paper comparison is not possible here. The table compares the two eligible experimental blocks without combining them.

The no-party block is presented only through marginal-mean figures lacking N and computational/inference details. Neither block fully reports allocation probabilities, sequence generation, participant flow, missing-data rules, multiplicity, exact marginal-mean construction, or all internal-validity threats.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, table bodies, table notes, figure bodies, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status when they appeared in the published main article. Table 1 and its note earned credit for model, unit, sample size, estimates, uncertainty, covariates/fixed effects, and clustering without requiring a redundant equation. Figures 2–3 earned credit for displayed marginal means and uncertainty bars, but not for unreported N or interval construction. Appendix pointers earned no substantive credit.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given the same evidentiary status. Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–5 received affirmative credit where they supplied conditions, coding, sample sizes, estimates, uncertainty, and contrast mapping. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose. Appendix pointers on PDF page 18 and in main-text notes were not treated as supplied evidence.

checks.finding: Credited for treatment levels and the fixed deaths/cases restriction; not credited for allocation probabilities or full assignment mechanics.
Credited for outcome equations, open-border reference, estimates, standard errors, and analysis Ns; not credited for an unstated standard-error calculation.
Credited for displayed estimands, contrasts, estimates, 95% intervals, and named bootstrap types; not credited for omitted bootstrap/CI implementation details.
Credited for the reported outcome-ordinality concern and model choice.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison of the two distinct randomized samples; no cross-paper synthesis is attempted in this one-paper session.
direct_comparison.finding: The UK and US experiments have identical reporting structures and therefore identical criterion scores. Country-specific tables separately report N, coefficients, and standard errors; shared methods and combined figures identify country panels and contrasts. Neither experiment reports allocation probabilities, assignment sequence generation, participant flow beyond recruited/analyzed totals, complete weight/covariate coding, missingness rules, multiplicity status, or full inference implementation.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figure/table bodies, figure/table notes, and footnotes were treated as equal main-article evidence. Figure 1's note earned credit for omitted category, scaling, robust SEs, and 95% CIs; Figure 2's note earned the same inference credit; Table 1's body and note earned credit for means, differences, scales, SEs, and cell sizes. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, appendix pointers on pp. 954, 956, 957–959 were not treated as supplying omitted details.

title: Prolonged contact does not reshape locals’ attitudes toward migrants in wartime settings
citation: Zhou, Yang-Yang, and Jason Lyall. 2025. American Journal of Political Science 69(1): 210–222. doi:10.1111/ajps.12862.

reviewed_pages.boundary_confirmation: All 13 PDF pages are the published main article. PDF page 13 ends with references, a Supporting Information availability notice, and the article citation; no supplementary pages are embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only, including main-text prose, tables, figures, table/figure notes, and footnotes. Online appendices, PAP/OSF, Dataverse materials, and external references were not used as paper-specific evidence.

consistency_audit.standard: The same binary full-reporting rule was applied to prose, tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. findings: Figures 2–5 received credit for reporting effect estimates and 90% confidence intervals because their axes, rows, panels, and notes visibly map outcomes and contrasts.
Tables 2–3 received credit for the quantities they actually report (model labels, standard errors, and Ns), but their subgroup/household Ns were not imputed to focal Figures 2–5.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, tables, figure notes, table notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Credit was awarded from Tables 4–7 and their notes for outcomes, model changes, N, estimates, and clustered robust SEs; no score was reduced merely because evidence was tabular. Appendix pointers were treated only as evidence that omitted material exists, not as evidence of its contents.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

findings: Tables and table notes were treated as evidence equal to prose: Table 5 earned credit for OLS, model terms, sample sizes, coefficients, standard errors, and state clustering.

title: Sources of Authoritarian Responsiveness: A Field Experiment in China

reviewed_pages.boundary_note: The PDF contains the complete published main article from title page 383 through references and the publisher's Supporting Information availability notice on printed page 400. No appendix tables or supplementary analyses are embedded in the PDF.

source_scope: Only article.pdf (published main article), including main-text prose, footnotes, Tables 1–4 and their notes, and Figures 1–6 and their notes. The online supporting information, preregistration, replication materials, cited works, and web sources were not consulted. English stimulus renderings were used only as printed; withheld Chinese originals were treated as missing.
inventory_note: One distinct randomized experiment was identified. No list experiment, supporting experiment with a new randomized sample/manipulation, brief diagnostic randomization, or outcome-free pilot appears in the main article. Random generation of form-fill identifiers is not an experimental assignment, and follow-up outcomes use the primary assignment.

experiments.name: Study 3 CCES regression-discontinuity and matching analysis
experiments.classification_rationale: The treatment is an observed close-election result described as “as good as random”; the researchers did not randomly assign an intervention. It is inventoried as observational/natural-experiment analysis and is not scored under the randomized-experiment criteria.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper session; comparison is across the paper’s experiments, not across papers.
direct_comparison.findings: Study 1 provides clearer outcome/estimand and factorial-model detail, including robust SE labels, while Study 2 provides clearer behavioral outcomes and raw baselines. Across all four experiments, sequence generation, complete participant flow, missingness/attrition handling, multiplicity/status, and fully specified variance estimation are absent. Study 2 additionally omits the exact emails from the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 supplied OLS, robust SEs, outcome direction, exclusions, and per-column N; Table 2 supplied OLS, estimates, SEs, controls status, constants, and per-column N. No score was reduced merely because support appeared in a display. Conversely, display labels such as “OLS” or “standard errors” did not receive credit for omitted implementation details. Pointers to online supporting information received no evidentiary credit.

experiments.name: Statewide pilot public-opinion surveys for issue selection
experiments.classification_rationale: Small Google Consumer Surveys were used to choose low-support issue positions. The main article reports no randomized manipulation or outcome analysis, so this is observational/design screening, not a scored experiment.

additional_checklist.note: No additional reporting checklist was supplied; this assessment is omitted as instructed.

direct_comparison.scope_note: Only one paper is in this independent session, so no cross-paper ranking is possible. Within-paper comparison is shown by experiment.

rows.summary: Study 1 has complete table-level analysis counts and traceability but lacks exact treatment materials, full randomization implementation, raw group quantities, multiplicity status, and CI construction.

Study 2's tables clearly specify OLS contrasts and clustered inference, but reporting is weakened by absent flow/allocation counts and the 1,047-versus-1,140 respondent conflict; exact treatment materials, raw group quantities, multiplicity status, and CI construction are also absent.

consistency_audit.standard: Main-text prose, tables, table notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. External appendix pointers received no credit.
findings: Tables 3–8 and their notes earned credit for estimators, outcomes, regressors, samples, coefficients, standard errors, and clustering wherever explicit; no redundant equation was required.

Study 2 contains an unresolved conflict: printed p. 215 reports 2,528 issue–respondent observations from 1,047 voters, while Table 7 on printed p. 216 reports 2,528 observations and 1,140 respondent clusters.
Pointers to Supplementary Appendices A–D did not supply exact letters, balance evidence, heterogeneity figures, questionnaires, or attrition details.
The Replication Materials notice on PDF page 1 and Supporting Information list on PDF page 14 were recorded as scope markers only, not evidence.

reviewed_pages.statement: The PDF contains exactly the published article from title/abstract through references and the publisher's Supporting Information availability list. All 17 PDF pages (printed 100–116) were reviewed; no supplement pages are embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only: article.pdf, with article.txt and pages.json used solely as extractions of that PDF. Supporting-information tables/figures, Dataverse materials, external references, and web sources were not used as paper-specific evidence.
inventory_note: One randomized experiment was identified. checks.detail: Table 1 note supplied the white base category and presence of standard errors.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment-level comparison only; cross-paper synthesis is reserved for the later independent-assessment stage.
direct_comparison.summary: All five experiments share the same principal transparency strengths (exact arm wording, respondent analysis unit, displayed logistic coefficients/robust SEs/N, and traceable model columns) and weaknesses (recruitment/flow, randomization implementation, incomplete coding, missingness, multiplicity, and simulation details). Experiments 1–3 additionally report raw arm percentages; Experiments 4–5 do not. Experiment 3 also omits the exact outcome recode.

findings: Tables 1–5 and their notes received the same evidentiary status as prose for estimator, covariates, interactions, robust standard errors, two-tailed tests, analysis N, coefficients, and uncertainty.
Figure notes received credit for identifying simulated 95% confidence intervals, but not for absent simulation algorithm, draw count, or interval construction.
Footnotes received full evidentiary status: footnote 8 supports the common four-point outcome and binary recode; footnote 6 limits mechanism identification.
Pointers to supporting information (sample demographics, module placement, differences in means, robustness checks) were recorded as pointers only and supplied no evidence for omitted content.

experiments.name: Birmingham partisan telephone mobilization spillover experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary randomized field experiment. One individual per two-voter household was assigned within party-preference blocks to high-intensity call, low-intensity call, or no-contact control. Direct, spillover, moderator, and CACE analyses all reuse this assignment; none is a new experiment.

rows.summary: Strong arm-level outcome reporting and extensive scope discussion, but exact scripts, randomization sequence, several model/inference details, and per-figure sample sizes are missing from the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables, figures, notes, footnotes, and prose were given equal evidentiary status. Figure 2 supplied allocation counts; Table 1 and its note supplied means, ITTs, N, weighting, and randomization-inference labels; Table 2 and its note supplied model columns, covariates, reference group, errors, and N. Scores were reduced only where those displays plus prose still omitted required information. Pointers to online Tables A1–A7, Figures A1–A5, equations, scripts, questionnaire, codebook, and replication files were not treated as evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

findings: Prose, main-text tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as coequal main-article evidence.

findings: Prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were eligible for identical evidentiary credit.
Table 4 and its note were inspected visually but concern observational issue rankings, not the list-experiment contrast; they were not substituted for missing experiment quantities.
The list-experiment arm means and p-value appear in prose and received the same credit they would have received in a table.
Footnote 17 received credit for the California confidence interval and for identifying the national replication, but not for unreported national arm means, uncertainty, or sample size.
Pointers to SI Items/Tables 4, SI-9, SI-10, and SI-11 did not receive credit for omitted content.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status when they appeared in the published main article. Tables 1–4 and their notes earned credit for estimator, covariates, robust SEs, N, effects, and traceability. Figure notes earned evidence credit for simulated 95% intervals but not for unreported simulation implementation. Pointers to Supporting Information earned no credit for omitted content.

checks.result: Equal status; no score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a table.

No substantive credit; PDF page 17 and footnote pointers identify SI but do not supply its contents.

title: How to Elect More Women: Gender and Candidate Success in a Field Experiment

reviewed_pages.main_article_boundary: PDF pages 1–17. Research article body runs through printed p. 941; references continue on pp. 941–942; pp. 942–943 contain only the publisher's Supporting Information availability/inventory, not the supplement itself.

source_scope: Only article.pdf (the published main article), including its main text, tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Online Supporting Information, replication materials, links, and external references were not used as evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

inventory_notes: Two distinct experiments were identified. The profile-feature randomizations are embedded in the same respondent sample and candidate-choice task as the vignette treatment and are mapped within that experiment, not counted as separate studies. No technical sensitive-item list experiment appears in the main article. The post-caucus compliance survey, observer subsample, and mechanism outcomes reuse the field assignment and therefore belong to the field experiment rather than constituting new experiments.

experiments.name: Study 3: ANES panel analyses of vote choice and changing evaluations
experiments.classification_rationale: Observational analysis: downstream vote and opinion models use measured implicit/explicit attitudes as predictors. Embedded AMP randomizations are separately inventoried as E3 and E4, but the substantive Study 3 estimates are not randomized treatment contrasts.

additional_checklist.note: No additional reporting checklist was supplied; separate checklist assessment omitted.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment-level comparison; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: Study 1 and Study 2 have equally transparent focal OLS models and Table 2 inference, but both omit randomization mechanics, exact instruments, missing-data rules, multiplicity status, and raw arm quantities. Study 2 additionally leaves two recruited participants and delayed-wave retention unexplained. The embedded AMP diagnostics describe score construction or assignment purpose but do not report complete randomized contrasts with uncertainty.

findings: Table 2 and its note received the same evidentiary status as prose: they support outcome scaling, treatment coding, subgroup sample sizes, coefficients, robust standard errors, and two-tailed tests.
Displayed equations on pp. 898, 901, and 902 were treated as main-article evidence; no redundant prose equation was required.
Table constants were not misclassified as raw treatment/control means.
Pointers to supporting information on pp. 896–904 and p. 907 were recorded only as evidence that material is absent from the main article, never as evidence that the omitted details were reported.
Figures and notes were accepted for coding/orientation where explicit; customary implementation was never inferred.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

experiments.name: German welfare-office multifactor correspondence (conjoint) experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary causal study: five email attributes were randomized across the 408-office census and formally analyzed with OLS/AMCE models. The 24-office pretest is retained as a separately inventoried pilot phase because its Turkish female alias and field date differ, although the article pools it into the primary analysis.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison only; cross-paper synthesis is reserved for the later independent-assessment synthesis.
direct_comparison.finding: All five experiments share nearly identical statistical transparency: OLS models, covariate progressions, analysis Ns, coefficients, and main-table alternative specifications are visible, but exact outcome coding, complete randomization details, missing-data rules, and table uncertainty procedures are not. Experiments 1–2 additionally provide a main-text party-interaction table; other additional checks are largely deferred to excluded supporting information.

consistency_audit.finding: Prose, figures, tables, table notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Tables 1–4 earned credit for OLS, covariate names, order adjustment, Ns, and coefficients. No credit was withheld merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, unlabeled parenthetical values were not assumed to be standard errors, and SI pointers were not treated as reporting omitted material.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figures, table/figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 earned experimental-condition credit; Figures 2–6 earned effect-and-uncertainty credit. Footnotes 8–10 were used to establish that constraints and external details exist, but appendix pointers did not supply omitted information. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared graphically or in a table, and no score was increased based on customary conjoint practice.

findings: Tables 1–3 and their notes received the same evidentiary status as prose.
Table 1 earned evidence for OLS, covariates, pooled N, coefficients, SEs, and reference coding, but not wave-specific results or an unnamed SE estimator.
Table 2's constants were treated as control means; its notes supported OLS and two-tailed inference.
Table 3 supported OLS/logit specifications, interactions, Ns, coefficients, and SEs; it could not resolve participant-flow inconsistencies or weighting/SE type.
Pointers to online appendices were treated only as evidence that main-article detail was absent.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; comparison is across experiments/classes, not across papers.
direct_comparison.summary: The main numbered Study 2 and Study 3 analyses are more statistically traceable than the separately scored Study 1 waves because Study 1 reports only a pooled model. article_comparison: Only one paper is in this independent session, so no cross-paper ranking is made. Within the article, Study 1 is statistically more transparent than Study 2 because it reports N, exact outcome coding, marginal arm means, and more model detail; neither experiment is fully reconstructable because the complete regressions and instruments are outside the main article.

findings: Main-text prose, Table 1, Figures 1–5, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as evidence on equal terms.
Figures 1–5 on PDF pages 7–11 were visually inspected against extracted text; plotted values/labels and notes were incorporated where legible.
No main-text regression table exists. Footnotes 19, 22, and 27 point to SI Table 3; those pointers were recorded as absence evidence, not as supplied methods.
The two Past Actions Ns in Figure 2 sum to Study 1 N=1,804; no Study 2 N appears in prose, Figure 5, its note, or footnotes.
Figure 4's note incorrectly refers to Iran although Figure 4 is the Study 1 result; scoring follows the surrounding Study 1 text and plotted Country A design.
Figure 5's note refers to panels (c) and (d) although the display has panels (a)–(c); this labeling inconsistency does not supply missing inferential details.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper comparison across separately scored experiments; no cross-paper synthesis was attempted.

rows.name: Dickson, Gordon, and Huber (2015) laboratory institutional-environment experiment (reanalysis)

direct_comparison.conclusion: The original judge experiment is more transparent than the DGH reanalysis on analysis N, outcome mapping, estimand, and confidence intervals. Neither experiment reports a reconstructable estimator and inference procedure; the DGH reanalysis additionally omits its modeled outcome, analysis unit, and sample size.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as equal main-article evidence. Table 2 received credit for its outcome note, covariates, column Ns, estimates, and visible specification changes; it did not receive inferred credit for an unnamed estimator or unlabeled parentheses. Table 3 received credit for contrast labels, period indicators, exclusion note, estimates, and specification changes; it did not receive credit for details deferred to supporting information or for customary interpretations of parentheses.

checks.finding: Used only for the observational literature-review inventory; not treated as a randomized experiment.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

title: Encouraging Political Voices of Underrepresented Citizens through Coproduction: Evidence from a Randomized Field Trial

reviewed_pages.statement: All 13 PDF pages (printed pp. 597–609) were reviewed. PDF p. 13 contains the end of the references and a publisher notice listing online supporting appendices; no appendix content is embedded in the PDF.

source_scope: Published main article only: main text, equations, Tables 1–4 and their notes, footnotes, and conclusion on PDF pp. 1–13 (printed pp. 597–609). Online Appendices A–F, replication materials, linked sources, and external references were excluded and supplied no evidence.
inventory_note: One distinct randomized experiment was identified. All outcomes and follow-ups reuse the same cluster assignment. No separate embedded list experiment, diagnostic randomization, pilot without outcome, or observational study was found. The nonvoter analysis is a post-assignment subgroup analysis within the original trial, not a new experiment.

experiments.name: Aarhus coproduction stratified cluster-randomized field trial
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment: 112 preschools were randomized within 12 strata to coproduction, SLB, or no-intervention control; the article's focal formal analyses estimate assignment effects on survey participation and municipal voting. Satisfaction, compliance, and voter-status analyses use the same original assignment and are not distinct experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, table bodies, table titles, and table notes were given equal evidentiary status. Tables 1–4 earned credit for arm counts, model Ns, outcome coding, estimator, fixed-effect/covariate inclusion, clustered standard errors, two-sided tests, coefficients, and uncertainty. consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes received the same evidentiary status. Full credit was awarded where displays jointly resolved an item (for example, Table 3 plus its note for estimator, reference outcome, N, estimates, and robust SEs). No credit was withheld merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, pointers to supporting information were not treated as evidence for omitted details.

findings: Main-text prose, tables, table notes, figure content, and footnotes were treated as equal evidence.

Table 2 and its continuation earned credit for the randomized cue levels and visible treatment variations, but not for complete stimulus reproducibility because the common newspaper story and all complete treatments are not printed.
Table 3 and its note earned full credit for estimator identity, displayed coefficients, standard errors, and column-specific sample sizes; prose was not required to duplicate them.

Table 3 did not earn credit for the standard-error estimator, clustering decision, weights, arm-specific counts, or raw group quantities because neither the table/note nor prose supplies those details.
Pointers to supporting information and replication materials were recorded only as pointers and supplied no evidence for omitted content.

direct_comparison.finding: The 2015 primary experiment is more transparent about raw group quantities because Figures 2–4 show arm means with labeled 95% confidence intervals. Both experiments provide coded factorial predictors and coefficient estimates, but neither reports allocation probabilities, exact stimuli, estimator, regression uncertainty procedure, focal analysis N, missing-data rules, or multiplicity handling. consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as equal main-article evidence. Tables 1–2 earned credit for enumerating scenario combinations; footnote 4 earned coding credit; Figure 2–4 notes earned credit for identifying 95% confidence intervals. Figures 5–6 did not earn inference-procedure credit because their error bars are unlabeled. Appendix pointers supplied no omitted evidence.
examples: Tables 1–2 were used for arm definitions.

findings: Prose, equations, tables, table notes, figure notes and footnotes received equal evidentiary weight.
Table 2 and its note earned credit for OLS, treatment coding, fixed-effect changes, clustering, sample sizes, estimates and standard errors without requiring a redundant equation.

The Table 2 top-panel row labeled ‘Sector FE’ in model 5 is interpreted with the accompanying text as province fixed effects; this display/text mismatch is recorded and does not supply missing heterogeneous-model covariates.
Pointers to SI Sections A, D–J were not treated as evidence for omitted methods or results.
Observed arm counts were not treated as intended assignment probabilities, and the phrase ‘randomized’ was not treated as a sequence-generation method.
Figure 4–5 histograms were not treated as exact sample-size reports.
consistency_audit.table_note_treatment: Table and figure notes were credited whenever they directly reported information; no credit was withheld merely because evidence appeared in a display.

statistical_transparency_comparison: Only one paper is in this independent session, so no cross-paper ranking is possible. Within AJPS127, the main Table 2 analysis is substantially more reconstructable than the heterogeneous-effect analyses in Figures 4–5: the former reports OLS, coding, fixed effects, clustered SEs, Ns, estimates and uncertainty, while the latter omit named covariates, exact Ns, and interval construction from the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as equal main-article evidence. Tables 1–3 earned credit for group means, ATE/CATE estimates, CIs, p-values, and sample sizes. They did not earn credit for unreported allocation, sequence generation, weighting, SE estimator, clustering, or CI construction. Figure 5 earned credit for graphically shown condition means and 95% CIs but not unprinted numerical values. SI pointers supplied no evidence.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.summary: Within this paper, the two focal sexual-harassment experiments are substantially more transparent than the diagnostic and robustness experiments because Tables 1–3 report raw quantities, effects, uncertainty, and n. Across all experiments, allocation/sequence generation and inference-construction details are the most persistent omissions.

source_scope: Published main article only: main text, Tables 1–4 and their notes, figure/table text, and footnotes on PDF pp. 1–14 (printed pp. 53–66). Online Supporting Information, replication materials, external references, and linked web content were not used as evidence.

direct_comparison.finding: Within this paper, E1 is materially more transparent because Tables 1–4 provide exact treatments, arm quantities, cell sizes, effects, and confidence intervals. E2–E4 are brief main-text generalizability summaries: each gives total recruited N and a point result, but not exact full treatments, analytic N, estimator implementation, arm quantities, or numerical uncertainty.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. E1 received credit from Table 1's treatment text and Tables 2–4's cell sizes, coding notes, effect definitions, estimates, and intervals. No score was reduced merely because evidence was tabular. Conversely, qualitative significance statements and pointers to Supporting Information did not substitute for omitted numerical uncertainty or implementation detail.

direct_comparison.scope: One-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: Within this article, E2 is the most numerically transparent because Table 5 supplies estimates, SEs, and analysis Ns. E1 and E3 report arm percentages but omit explicit randomized contrasts, contrast uncertainty, and analysis Ns. All three omit sequence generation, experiment-specific missingness, and a fully specified inference procedure.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, tables, table notes, and footnotes received identical evidentiary status when they were inside the main article. Table 5 earned credit for its displayed conditions, bases, estimates, SEs, and Ns; it did not earn inferred credit for an unnamed estimator, weights, or SE calculation. Figure 7 earned credit for displayed arm quantities, but not for unreported arm Ns or uncertainty. SI/appendix pointers supplied no evidence.

direct_comparison.finding: All three country experiments have the same statistical-transparency profile because the main article reports them through the same figures and shared method description. findings: Main-text prose, figures, figure labels, footnotes, and notes were treated as equal-capacity evidence.
Figures 1–5 received credit for reporting effect estimates and 95% confidence intervals even though the same values were not repeated in prose.
Footnote 22 received credit for the 0–1 transformation; footnote 20 received evidence status for weighting, while its ambiguity prevented full specification credit.
Pointers to SI Appendixes A–J were recorded as pointers only and never treated as supplying omitted content.
No regression-table penalty was applied: the main article contains no main-text regression table to evaluate.

direct_comparison.summary: The factorial estimand/model and coding are clear in the main text, but exact stimuli, randomization implementation, analysis Ns, weighting, missingness, multiplicity, uncertainty construction, and mechanism-scope limits are not reconstructable or explicit.

findings: Table 1 received the same evidentiary status as prose: its four arm counts supported randomized-cell counts and group structure.
Figure 1 and its note received the same evidentiary status as prose: they supported outcome-to-estimator mapping, group predictions, marginal-effect mapping, and displayed uncertainty.
No credit was withheld merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.
Conversely, unlabeled error bars could not establish an SE/CI procedure, and pointers to supporting information could not supply excluded detail.

source_scope: Published main article only: prose, footnotes, Table 1, Figures 1–4 and their notes, and Equation 5. Online SI, registry, replication materials, web sources, and cited external methods were excluded.

experiments.name: PITI public-disclosure field experiment

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: Within this article, Studies 1–3 have similar transparency: their arms, outcomes, assignment unit, estimands, analysis units, coding, and plotted group quantities are identifiable, but sample flow, allocation process, complete model implementation, dependence adjustment, effect uncertainty, and main-text robustness details are not. The Supreme Court diagnostic is markedly less transparent because it reports only a 15/18 directional tally without arm Ns, effects, or uncertainty. Study 3 provides more named tests (F-test p-values) and more arms, but still lacks the information needed to reproduce its inference.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figure notes, table notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figure 1–5 notes supported coding, contrasts, group quantities, and reported test statistics; Table 1 and its note supported the separate observational inventory. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, the display notes did not receive credit for unreported model terms, variance estimators, Ns, or dependence handling. SI pointers on PDF pages 5–7, 10–12, and 15 received no evidentiary credit.

direct_comparison.scope_note: This independent session covers one paper, so cross-paper ranking is not possible. The table compares statistical transparency across its experiments without averaging experiment classes.
direct_comparison.summary: Study 4 is most reconstructable because the main text states its saturated LPM and Figure 6 supplies robust SEs and N. Studies 1–3 defer full models to SI and omit at least one focal analysis N. All four omit allocation probabilities/sequence generation, complete flow, analysis status, and CI construction.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figures, table/figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 and Figure 6 notes earned affirmative component evidence where complete; SI pointers earned no credit. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display note rather than prose.
checks: Table 1 and its note supplied dates, N, provider, outcomes, and target population.
Figure notes supplied estimator labels, contrasts, confidence intervals, robust SEs, and analysis Ns where present.

arms.anchor: 95 were presented with easy scenarios, and 106 were presented with hard scenarios
arms.paraphrase: The 201-person sample yielded 95 easy-scenario and 106 hard-scenario assignments.

experiments.name: Arab Barometer income and trust analyses
experiments.classification_rationale: Cross-sectional observational regressions of income and trust in Islamist parties; no randomized assignment.

experiments.name: Tunisian district unemployment and Ennahda vote-share analyses
experiments.classification_rationale: District-level observational electoral analysis; no randomized assignment.

inventory_note: No embedded list experiment, brief diagnostic randomization, or outcome-free pilot was identified in the main article. The post-treatment ‘Voting to Please God’ questions are survey measures within Experiment 2, not list-experiment randomizations.

additional_checklist.reason: No additional reporting checklist was supplied; no separate checklist was scored.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment comparison; cross-paper synthesis is deferred because this independent session assesses one paper.
direct_comparison.summary: Experiment 1 reports reproducible conditions and subgroup sample sizes but not its matched estimator/variance implementation. Experiment 2A improves outcome coding and participant flow but omits three scenario wordings and its focal estimator. Experiment 2B has the clearest regression display (Table 4), yet the central parallel-mediation computation, Figure 8 sample size, resampling/CI method, and sequential-cohort assignment details remain unreconstructable.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Table 4 earned evidence for OLS coefficients, standard errors, constants, column-specific N, and specification changes. Figure notes earned evidence for reference groups and confidence levels. No display was used to infer an unstated variance estimator, randomization algorithm, missing-data rule, or mediation computation. SI pointers were recorded only as evidence of main-article absence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

title: The Moderating Effect of Debates on Political Attitudes

reviewed_pages.boundary_note: All 19 PDF pages are the published article. PDF page 19 ends the references and carries only a Supporting Information availability/index notice; no appendix content is embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only, including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Online appendices, plan, registry, replication materials, and external references were excluded as evidence.

inventory_summary.list_experiment_note: No randomized list/item-count experiment is reported. Footnote 19's 'count measure' is an alternative partisanship measure, not a list experiment.

experiments.name: Five-arm parliamentary-debate field experiment (including two-day follow-up)
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary causal study: 1,991 participants were individually randomized among four debate exposures and a placebo. The random 10% two-day survey reused original assignment, so it belongs to E1 rather than constituting a new experiment.

experiments.name: Three-task hypothetical-candidate policy conjoint experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment. This is the article's central randomized conjoint: the same 6,070-person survey generates three randomized candidate-choice tasks per respondent. The respondent-specific issue draw, profile-level draws, and response-option polarity are design randomizations within this one experiment, not new randomized samples or separately analyzed experiments. No embedded list experiment was found.

experiments.name: Cross-national manifesto rhetoric and copartisan turnout analysis
experiments.classification_rationale: Manifesto rhetoric and survey turnout are observationally linked; no randomized assignment is reported.

experiments.name: 2015 British Election Study panel analysis of positive emotions and mobilization
experiments.classification_rationale: Positive emotions were measured rather than randomized; logistic regressions relate them to later turnout and activism.

findings: Main-text prose, Figure 3, its note, and footnotes 19–23 were given the same evidentiary status.
Figure 3 received credit for graphical effect estimates and 95% confidence intervals, but its absence of analysis-specific Ns and CI construction was scored as missing.
Table 2 was reviewed but belongs to the observational BES panel analysis and was not used to score the randomized experiments.
Pointers to SI6 and the printed-page-355 supporting-information notice were treated only as evidence that details are absent from the main article, not as evidence that those details were reported.

evidence.anchor: Each point indicates the estimated difference in means
evidence.paraphrase: Figure 3 plots point estimates and 95% confidence intervals for pooled, Labour, and Conservative results; values are graphical rather than tabulated.

evidence.anchor: Additional supporting information may be found online
evidence.paraphrase: Printed page 355 is only a contents notice for online appendices; those excluded materials were not treated as evidence.

comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis deferred.
comparison.finding: Within this paper, Labour is more reproducible than Conservative because its vignette is printed in full. Both formal experiments identify a difference-in-means estimand and graph effects with 95% CIs, but neither reports allocation details, participant flow, inference construction, missingness rules, multiplicity handling, arm means, or analysis-specific Ns. The out-partisan diagnostics are not statistically reconstructable from the main article.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

title: Universal Love or One True Religion? Experimental Evidence of the Ambivalent Effect of Religious Ideas on Altruism and Discrimination

reviewed_pages.boundary_basis: The PDF contains 18 consecutive journal article pages, beginning with title/abstract and ending with references/supporting-information notice; no appendix pages are embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–18 (printed 603–620), including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Appendix/SI, verification materials, web sources, and external methodological references were excluded.
inventory_note: One scored randomized experiment was found. No list experiment appears in the main article. The one-shot prisoner's dilemma mentioned in footnote 9 reused the experimental session/assignment and reports no outcome; under the follow-up rule it remains an unreported secondary outcome within Experiment E1, not a separate experiment.

experiments.name: Three-arm religious-prime dictator game with randomized receiver order
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment supporting the article's principal causal claims. Participants were randomized to one of three primes and to the order of same- versus different-religion dictator-game recipients; formal analyses appear in Tables 3–5 and Figures 2–3.

title: Moderation and Competence: How a Party’s Ideological Position Shapes Its Valence Reputation
citation: Johns, Robert, and Ann-Kristin Kölln. 2020. American Journal of Political Science 64(3): 649–663. doi:10.1111/ajps.12481.

reviewed_pages.boundary_confirmation: The supplied 15-page PDF is the continuous published article from printed page 649 through 663. Page 15 contains the end of the references and a Supporting Information availability list; the linked/online items were not consulted.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–15, including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Online SI Table A1, Figures A1–A3, full questionnaire, verification materials, and all external sources were excluded.
inventory_note: One scored randomized experiment was identified. The paper’s plural ‘conjoint experiments’ refers to repeated paired tasks/outcomes within the same respondent sample and assignment design, not distinct randomized samples. No list experiment appears in the main article.

experiments.name: Paired choice-based conjoint experiment on hypothetical party profiles
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary randomized experiment: respondents completed two paired-profile tasks with randomized attribute levels; competence choice is explicitly primary, with ratings and post-treatment mechanism outcomes using the same assignments.

direct_comparison: Within this single-paper review, Study 2 names OLS and covariates more clearly, while Study 1 explicitly reports subject-clustered errors for its pooled panel model. Both omit exact stimulus wording, allocation procedures, full focal specifications, complete analysis Ns, and general SE/CI construction, so neither statistical analysis is fully reconstructable from the main article alone.

findings: Figures and figure notes received the same evidentiary status as prose: Figure 1 supplied 0/1 personality coding, randomization timing, and 95% CIs; Figure 4 supplied candidate coding, subgroup mapping, and 95% CIs.

The article contains no main-text regression tables. A regression equation was not demanded; scores fell where prose plus figures/notes did not identify complete models, samples, coding, or inference.
Pointers to SI Appendices A.1–A.15 were treated only as evidence that details are absent from the main article, never as evidence that those details were reported in scope.
No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper ranking is not applicable in this session.

rows.summary: Strongest on explicit contrasts, analysis unit, numerical effects/CIs, and inferential-scope caveats; weakest on allocation mechanics, full treatment texts, participant flow, exact model/inference implementation, missingness, raw arm quantities, and internal-validity threats.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, tables, table notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Tables 4–5 earned credit for observation counts, village fixed effects, village clustering, bootstrap replication count, FDR handling, estimates, and p-values. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, a table label or SI pointer did not receive credit for omitted estimator, reference-category, confidence-interval, treatment-text, or missing-data details.

records.paraphrase: Table 4 reports estimates, p-values, 490 observations, village fixed effects, village-level clustering, wild bootstrap with 1,000 replications, and FDR-controlled p-values for non-index outcomes.
Table 5 reports separate Dinka and Nuer regressions with 256 and 234 observations and the same fixed-effect/inference notes.
